title: Same-number faith with/without charity is common teaching, not defined dogma like same-species
source_text: XIII. Imo communis Scholae Romanae doctrina est eandem numero fidem modo formatam & vivam, modo mortuam & informem esse posse. Nempe Petri fides eadem in se & intrinsece manens, alias fides informis & mortua dicitur absente charitate, alias vero fides viva & formata si charitas adsit. Sed prior sententia quae statuit fidem vivam & mortuam ad eandem fidei speciem pertinere, est in Ecclesia Romana definita, & inter dogmata fidei recensetur: Posterior vero quae ponit eandem numero fidem modo formatam, modo informem esse, non est paris certitudinis, nec tanquam dogma fidei habetur: & contrarium tenuerunt quidam veteres Scholastici, licet Doctores hodierni calculo suo illam communiter approbent.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed the common doctrine of the Roman School is that the same faith in number can sometimes be formed and living, sometimes dead and unformed. Namely Peter's faith, remaining the same in itself and intrinsically, is sometimes called unformed and dead faith when charity is absent, but sometimes living and formed faith if charity is present. But the prior sentence which establishes that living and dead faith belong to the same species of faith is defined in the Roman Church and is reckoned among the dogmas of faith: But the posterior which posits that the same faith in number is sometimes formed, sometimes unformed, is not of equal certainty, nor is it held as a dogma of faith: and some older Scholastics held the contrary, although today's Doctors commonly approve it by their vote.
pass_b_english: Common Roman teaching even allows the same numerical faith to be formed or unformed as charity comes and goes — Peter's faith intrinsically the same under either label.
Same-species living/dead faith is defined dogma; same-number continuity is common and approved by modern doctors, but not equal in certainty and not a dogma — some older Scholastics opposed it.

lemmas.gloss: is reckoned among the dogmas of faith
